candidates.text: Upon this ground, we have not the slightest hesitation in holding that, under and in virtue of the Constitution, the owner of a slave is clothed with entire authority
candidates.speaker: Story
phrases: to seize and recapture his slave whenever he can do it without any breach of the peace
candidates.reason: States the case's central rule: a self-executing constitutional right of peaceable recaption that voids obstructing state law.

candidates.text: The clause manifestly contemplates the existence of a positive, unqualified right on the part of the owner of the slave
candidates.speaker: Story
phrases: positive, unqualified right on the part of the owner of the slave
candidates.reason: The preemption premise (any state law that delays recaption is a pro tanto discharge) that Finkelman and Holden-Smith treat as the opinion's pro-slavery core.

candidates.text: As to the authority so conferred upon state magistrates, while a difference of opinion has existed, and may exist still
candidates.speaker: Story
phrases: state magistrates may, if they choose, exercise that authority
candidates.reason: Non-compulsion principle that spurred personal liberty laws and later anti-commandeering doctrine.

candidates.text: The language used in the Constitution does not, in my judgment, justify this construction given to it by the court
candidates.speaker: Taney
phrases: forbidden to make any regulation that shall impair it, but there the prohibition stops

candidates.text: In a state where slavery is allowed, every coloured person is presumed to be a slave
candidates.speaker: McLean
phrases: in a non-slaveholding state, every person is presumed to be free
